requirements.requirement: Enable a persistent host firewall on node1.
requirements.summary: IPv4 and IPv6 rules and a network pre-up restoration hook were installed and active. After an acknowledged node1 restart with a changed boot identity, the saved hashes, DROP policies, scoped rules, SSH service, and traffic behavior were recovered.

requirements.requirement: Allow SSH to node1 from any address.
requirements.summary: The final IPv4 and IPv6 rules allow TCP/22 from unrestricted source ranges. Connectivity succeeded from both node2 and node3 before and after node1 restarted, and node1's SSH listener remained healthy.

requirements.requirement: Allow TCP port 9000 only from node2 and reject it from node3 and all other sources.
requirements.summary: The final IPv4 policy accepts port 9000 only from node2's address and then applies a catch-all TCP reset rejection; IPv6 has only the catch-all rejection. With a bounded test listener, node2 received the expected response while node3 was refused, both before and after node1 restarted. Final rule counters recorded hits on both paths.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use legacy-compatible software.
requirements.summary: Node1 remained Ubuntu 7.10 with kernel 2.6.22-14-generic. The solution used the platform's existing iptables 1.3.6, kernel modules, and ifupdown pre-up hook rather than changing the OS or kernel.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. The firewall policy was directly inspected and behaviorally tested, including across a node1 restart. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed coherently on all three nodes: pre-restart health and identities, acknowledgements, distinct post-restart identities, and recovered network/SSH plus applicable scoped traffic behavior were captured and agree with the fixed lifecycle observations.
limitations: Behavioral rejection was directly tested from node3, while rejection from every other possible address is established by the final catch-all IPv4/IPv6 rules rather than exhaustive source-by-source probes.

The lifecycle collector could not inspect failed services because systemctl is unsupported on this legacy release; direct SysV-era service, process, socket, and connectivity checks provide the relevant health evidence instead.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutation was identified. Loading legacy netfilter modules and installing the rule files/hook directly supported the firewall outcome. Temporary port-9000 listeners were bounded verification fixtures and were removed; final evidence and the lifecycle snapshot show no temporary-file or listener residue. Each node restart served the mandatory provider restart protocol, with acknowledged restarts, changed boot identities, and recovered SSH/network and applicable firewall behavior. Package-health observations did not change.
